page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text on the left; a column of marginal notes in the right margin, beside the first lines of the text. Below the text, a short run of Italian prayer text (Oratio Dominica Italice) continues to the foot of the column.

main_text.p: ꝗISLANDI lingua utuntur Cimbrica siue Danica.
ꝗISMAELITICA lingua, vide supra in Æthiopum lingua ex Munstero.

ꝗITALORVM lingua à Latina vetere corrupta est, ut diximus. Barbarorum infestatione & imperio Dialecti ejus plures sunt: inter quas Thuscam (id est, in Hetruria circa Senas præcipuè) præferri ajunt: versus alpes quo propiùs habitant Itali (nam & Gallos Cisalpinos omnes hodie Italos vocamus) eò minùs purè loquuntur. Ineptissimus & maximè depravatus Rhætorum in alpibus sermo est, de quo in R. elemento scribemus. Romanorum sermonem non modò Itali suum vocant: sed etiam Sabaudi vulgò, & Rhęti alpini. Valachis etiam Romanus est sermo (ut Athenæus Pius refert) sed magna ex parte mutatus & homini Italico vix intelligibi-lis. Gregorium Papam suæ ecclesiæ adhuc Latinè locutum constat.Italica lin-gua à Latinâ vetere corrupta.
main_text.head: Oratio Dominica Italice.
main_text.p: Padre nostro, che sei ne cieli: Sia santifi-cato tuo nome: Venga il tuo regno: Sia fatta la tua volontà, si come in cielo, cosi ancora in terra. Dacci hoggi il nostro pane cotidia-no: E rimettici i nostri debiti, si come ancor

page.notes: Right margin note reads "Italica lin-gua à Latinâ vetere corrupta." (set in italic, placed beside the paragraph). The final lines of the Lord's Prayer are damaged by ink/bleed and partly obscured ("rimettici i nostri debiti" is partly illegible); the transcription there is best reading. Words marked [?] were not fully certain: none were marked beyond the damaged final line, which is set as read. The Italian and Latin text of the margin note is set in italic type. Right edge of page shows bleed-through from the reverse side, not transcribed.
